title: Reticulocyte count

review.note: Drafted from the source below; not yet reviewed by a medical professional.

measures: A reticulocyte count measures the number of reticulocytes in your blood. Reticulocytes are immature, still-developing red blood cells, so the count helps check whether the bone marrow is making the right amount of red blood cells.
context: The count can be higher during pregnancy and may rise for a short time after moving to a high altitude, returning to usual once the body adjusts. Some medicines can raise or lower it, and one result alone does not mean a condition.
aboveRange: Can be associated with hemolytic anemia, when red blood cells are broken down faster than the bone marrow can replace them
New or ongoing bleeding, as the body makes more red blood cells to replace what was lost
Higher counts during pregnancy or for a short time at high altitude
belowRange: Can be associated with iron deficiency anemia, the most common type of anemia
Can be associated with pernicious anemia, linked to not getting or not absorbing enough B vitamins
Can be associated with aplastic anemia or bone marrow that is not making enough blood cells
Can be associated with kidney conditions or cirrhosis of the liver
nextStep: Discuss this result with your doctor.
